title: What happens when you prompt an LLM
summary: Follow one question from your keyboard to the model and back, token by token.

steps.label: prompt
steps.title: You type a question
steps.text: Nothing smart has happened yet. The app just holds your text and the conversation so far.

steps.label: POST /v1/messages
steps.title: The app sends an HTTPS request
steps.text: Chat apps are thin clients. Every turn, they send the whole conversation again, because the model itself keeps no memory between calls.
payload: Hard cap on how long the answer can be.
The full chat history, oldest first.

steps.label: tokens
steps.title: Text becomes tokens
steps.text: Models read numbers, not letters. A tokenizer splits text into chunks (roughly ¾ of a word each) and maps every chunk to an ID.
payload: Common words are one token; rare ones split.
Input tokens are what you pay for on the way in.

steps.label: next token…
steps.title: The model predicts one token at a time
steps.text: For each position it scores every possible next token, picks one (temperature controls how adventurous), appends it, and repeats until it decides to stop.
payload: Probabilities for the very first output token.
0 = always the top choice, higher = more variety.
The two ways a reply ends.

steps.label: stream (SSE)
steps.title: Tokens stream back as they're made
steps.text: That's why replies appear word by word. The API pushes small server-sent events instead of waiting for the full answer.
payload: One small chunk of new text.
Appended to what's already on screen.
Sent last: the model finished on its own.

steps.label: answer
steps.title: You read the answer
steps.text: One request, one response. Everything an agent does is built from repeating this loop with extra context and tools.
payload: "A webhook is a URL another app calls the moment something happens."
